questions.q: You want to train XGBoost on a CSV file using the SageMaker built-in algorithm. How must the CSV be laid out?
options: Header row first, label in the last column
Label in the first column and no header row
One JSON object per line
Features only, with the label in a separate file
questions.explain: For CSV training input the built-in algorithm assumes the target is the first column, and the CSV must not have a header record. You also set the content type to text/csv.

questions.q: You need one extra Python library that a pre-built scikit-learn image does not include. What does the AWS guide suggest trying first?
options: Building a completely new container from scratch
Switching to a built-in algorithm
Adding a requirements.txt next to your script, since that framework supports it
Copying the library into /opt/ml/model
questions.explain: Several frameworks, scikit-learn among them, install packages from a requirements.txt at runtime. Extending or building an image is for when that is not enough.

questions.q: In a bring-your-own training container, how does the program tell SageMaker the job failed?
options: It sends an email to the account owner
It deletes /opt/ml/model
It prints the word FAILED to standard output
It exits with a non-zero exit code, optionally writing details to /opt/ml/output/failure
questions.explain: Exit code 0 becomes Completed and any non-zero code becomes Failed. The failure file's first 1,024 characters are returned as the FailureReason.

questions.q: Inside a custom container, hyperparameters.json contains {"C": "0.5"}. What must your program do with the value?
options: Convert it, because every hyperparameter value arrives as a string
Nothing; it is already a float
Ignore it, since hyperparameters only work with built-in algorithms
Re-upload it to S3
questions.explain: The hyperparameters file holds string values, so your code must cast them to float or int itself.

questions.q: Which is the best reason to choose bring-your-own container over script mode on a pre-built image?
options: It is always cheaper
Your framework or language has no pre-built SageMaker image
Script mode cannot read data from S3
Custom containers skip the IAM role
questions.explain: Custom containers exist for cases the pre-built images cannot cover, such as a custom framework. They cost more maintenance, so they are a last resort.
